evals.prompt: i need a personal portfolio landing page. im a creative developer named Alex Rivers. want it to feel like an awwwards site — dark, big type, something alive in the background, buttery smooth scroll, tasteful entrance animations. no build tools please, just static files i can drop on netlify and open locally with no internet. put a hero, a short about blurb, 3 selected-work cards, and a contact footer with social icons.
evals.expected_output: Self-contained static site (index.html + local css/js assets). Animated background (one WebGL canvas max), smooth scrolling, entrance animations with prefers-reduced-motion fallback, consistent icon family, zero external network dependencies.
assertions: Offline-complete: no runtime resource is loaded from the network — no external script src, stylesheet href, font/url() or image URL in any delivered file (social profile links are fine)
All requested sections present: hero with the name Alex Rivers, about blurb, exactly 3 selected-work cards, contact footer with social icons
Animated background exists (WebGL canvas or CSS-animated) and at most ONE canvas/WebGL instance is created
Smooth scrolling implemented via a real mechanism (bundled Lenis or equivalent JS, or CSS scroll-behavior with easing work), not just default browser scroll
Entrance animations present AND gated behind a prefers-reduced-motion fallback (media query or JS matchMedia)
Social icons are a single consistent family of inline SVGs (same viewBox/stroke style), not emoji or mixed sources
If Animista keyframes were copied into the CSS, the FreeBSD license notice ships alongside them; pass as N/A if no Animista CSS used
Page opens without errors: valid HTML structure, every locally referenced asset file actually exists in the output directory

evals.prompt: build a landing page for 'Driftboard' — an AI meeting-notes tool for remote teams. dark mode, premium feel, animated but tasteful. needs: hero, logo strip of customers, 3 feature cards, a stats row, pricing with 3 tiers, footer. react + tailwind, next.js app-router style files. dont install anything or run a build — just write the files, and include a NOTES.md that lists every npm dep i need to install and any css that must go in globals.css.
evals.expected_output: page.tsx + section components + globals.css additions + NOTES.md with complete dep list. All 6 sections present, central color tokens, one icon family, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, imports consistent with NOTES.md deps.
assertions: All 6 requested sections present: hero, customer logo strip, exactly 3 feature cards, stats row, pricing with exactly 3 tiers, footer
NOTES.md exists and its dep list is COMPLETE: every non-react/next/local import used anywhere in the delivered code appears in NOTES.md
Color system is centralized (CSS custom properties or Tailwind theme tokens defined once); section files reference tokens rather than each defining their own ad-hoc palette
One icon family only across the whole page (no mixing lucide + radix + heroicons + inline one-offs)
Stats row numbers animate (count-up/ticker) triggered on scroll into view, not on mount
Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion (CSS media query, matchMedia, or the animation lib's reducedMotion config)
Required globals.css additions (keyframes/theme vars needed by any used component) are actually provided in the delivered globals.css content
Client/server component hygiene: every file using hooks or event handlers carries 'use client'

Arsenal-miss handled: the pricing tiers are hand-built — no import references a vendor/registry component that does not exist in the arsenal (pricing tables are not vendored, so a hallucinated pricing-component import fails this)

evals.prompt: here's my analytics dashboard component (StatsPanel.tsx). it works but feels dead. add micro-interactions and polish — hover states, number count-up animations, smooth staggered reveals, nicer status indicators. keep it professional, this is a b2b fintech app. don't redesign the layout or change the data/api shape, just bring it to life. include a NOTES.md listing new npm deps if any.
evals.expected_output: Updated StatsPanel.tsx preserving structure/exports/data shape; count-up on stats, subtle hovers and staggered reveals ≤300ms, reduced-motion handling, no backgrounds/WebGL added, NOTES.md with deps.
assertions: Structure preserved: default export StatsPanel remains, the 4 stat cards and the transactions table are still present, STATS/TXNS data shapes and the simulated-fetch pattern are unchanged
Number count-up animation on the stat values (not just a CSS fade), formatting preserved (currency/locale/suffix)
Staggered reveal on cards and/or table rows with per-item interaction durations ≤ 300ms and modest stagger gaps (≤ 100ms per item)
Hover states added to stat cards, table rows, and the Export button
Status indicators upgraded beyond bare colored text (e.g. dot/badge/pill), still readable and professional
NO decorative background, WebGL, canvas, gradient mesh, or page-level animation added — restraint appropriate for b2b fintech
Reduced-motion handled: prefers-reduced-motion media query, matchMedia, or the animation lib's built-in reduced-motion support
NOTES.md exists and every new non-react import in the delivered code appears in its dep list (or it states zero deps and code uses none)
